definition.def: The format of something is the way or order in which it is arranged and presented.
examples: I had met with him to explain the format of the programme and what we had in mind. [+ of]

definition.def: The format of a piece of computer software or a musical recording is the type of equipment on which it is designed to be used or played. For example, possible formats for a musical recording are CD and cassette.
examples: His latest album is available on all formats.

definition.def: To format a computer disk means to run a program so that the disk can be written on. [computing]
To format a piece of computer text or graphics means to arrange the way in which it appears when it is printed or is displayed on a screen. [computing]
examples: The saved text was often badly formatted with many short lines. [be VERB-ed]

examples.sentence: He says that while there is no single format for jokes, many revolve around a sudden and surprising conceptual shift.
The content and format of explanations dated back to a time when the museum was the exclusive domain of the scientific researcher.
You will hear a woman phoning a company that converts old photographs to digital format.
And I'd like to get them converted to digital format.
Yeah, but that was only in the UK, in the USA, programs or rather playbills continued to be published in the same format.
